children: WW International named Stephen Bye as its president and chief executive, effective this fall.

Bye's appointment comes after Tara Comonte resigned from the top role earlier this year. The weight-loss platform never named an interim CEO, choosing instead to have a committee of executives oversee its operations.

The company, also known as Weight Watchers, said Bye is a veteran of the consumer subscription business, having spent more than three decades leading companies through periods of significant industry disruption, evolving customer expectations and technological change.

Bye steps into WW International's top role as the company copes with the rise of weight-loss drugs. With the drugs dragging down demand for its dieting and food points program, Weight Watchers has pivoted to incorporate GLP-1s into its platform.

"Weight Watchers is at an important moment," Bye said. "What excites me most is the opportunity to bring together Weight Watchers' proven behavioral approach, clinical care and access to GLP-1 medications with technology and an increased focus on data-driven results to create a truly integrated and personalized weight health experience."

Bye most recently served as president and chief executive of Ookla, a global connectivity intelligence company whose brands include Speedtest, Downdetector, RootMetrics and Ekahau. Prior, he held senior leadership roles at companies including DISH Network, Connectivity Wireless, C Spire and Sprint.
